21.name: FTP (Unencrypted File Transfer)
21.description: Files transferred to or from this device travel over the network without encryption.
21.action: Disable FTP in the device settings or switch to secure file transfer options (SFTP/HTTPS).

23.name: Telnet (Unencrypted Remote Access)
23.description: This device accepts passwords over cleartext, making it vulnerable to interception on local Wi-Fi.
23.action: Disable Telnet in the device configuration menu and turn on SSH if remote access is required.

80.name: HTTP (Unencrypted Web Interface)
80.description: The device's control page is unencrypted. Logging in over guest Wi-Fi could expose admin credentials.
80.action: Enable HTTPS in your device settings or avoid accessing this admin page over untrusted connections.

445.name: SMB (Shared Network Drives)
445.description: Folders or drives are shared across the network, potentially exposing personal files to other devices.
445.action: Ensure password protection is enabled for all shared folders, or turn off file sharing if unused.

554.name: RTSP (Live Video Streaming)
554.description: A live camera feed is accessible over the local network without strong security protections.
554.action: Set a unique, strong password in your security camera settings to prevent unauthorized local viewing.

8080.name: Alternative Web Admin Panel
8080.description: A secondary web configuration page was found open on this device.
8080.action: Check if default login credentials (like admin/admin) are still active and update them immediately.

22.name: SSH (Secure Remote Access)
22.description: A secure remote-access door is open. That is fine if you use it, but it is a target if the password is weak.
22.action: If you do not use remote access, switch SSH off in the device settings. If you do, use a strong password or a key.

139.name: NetBIOS (Old Windows Sharing)
139.description: An old file-sharing service is on, which can reveal device names and shared folders.
139.action: Turn off NetBIOS / legacy file sharing in the device's network settings if you do not need it.

1883.name: MQTT (Smart-Home Messaging)
1883.description: A smart-home messaging service is open, and these often need no password at all.
1883.action: Set a username and password on the hub or MQTT service, or switch it off if unused.

3389.name: Remote Desktop
3389.description: Someone could take over this computer's screen remotely if they guess the password.
3389.action: Turn off Remote Desktop in Windows settings unless you really need it, and never expose it to the internet.

5555.name: Android Debug Bridge (Developer Back Door)
5555.description: A developer debugging door is open, which can let anyone on your Wi-Fi install apps or take control.
5555.action: Turn off USB debugging / ADB over network in Developer options.

5900.name: VNC (Screen Sharing)
5900.description: Screen sharing is switched on, often with a weak or missing password.
5900.action: Turn off screen sharing, or set a strong password on it.

7547.name: TR-069 (Router Remote Management)
7547.description: A remote-management service is open. It has been used in large attacks on home routers.
7547.action: Turn off remote management / TR-069 in the router admin page and update its firmware.

9100.name: Raw Printing
9100.description: This printer accepts print jobs from any device on your network without a login.
9100.action: Turn on access control or switch off raw printing if you do not use it.

upnp.name: UPnP (Automatic Port Opening)
upnp.description: This device lets other devices open doors in your router without asking you.
upnp.action: Turn off UPnP in your router settings unless a game or app really needs it.

cert_expired.name: Expired Security Certificate
cert_expired.description: A web page on this device has an expired security certificate, so browsers cannot trust it.
cert_expired.action: Check for a firmware update or renew the certificate in the device settings.

cert_selfsigned.name: Unverified Security Certificate
cert_selfsigned.description: This device uses a home-made security certificate, so a browser cannot prove who it is.
cert_selfsigned.action: Common and low-risk at home. Install firmware updates and log in only from your own devices.

wifi_open.name: Wi-Fi With No Password
wifi_open.description: The Wi-Fi network is open, so anyone in range can join it and watch the traffic.
wifi_open.action: Log in to the router, open Wireless settings and set security to WPA2 or WPA3 with a strong password.

wifi_weak.name: Outdated Wi-Fi Security
wifi_weak.description: The Wi-Fi uses outdated security (WEP or WPA1) that can be broken in minutes.
wifi_weak.action: Log in to the router, open Wireless settings and switch security to WPA2 or WPA3.
